Parittattika (The Triplet on the Limited)
Section on Analysis:
Root Condition.
Dependent upon a limited state, a limited state arises by way of root condition—dependent upon one limited aggregate.

Dependent on one limited aggregate, arise three aggregates and mind-produced matter … dependent on two aggregates … At the moment of rebirth-linking, dependent on one limited aggregate, arise three aggregates and kamma-produced matter … dependent on two aggregates … dependent on aggregates, arises the [heart-]base;
dependent on the base, arise the aggregates; dependent on one great primary, arise three great primaries.
… pe … dependent on two great primary elements (mahābhūta), mind-originated matter arises … pe ….

Dependent on a limited state (paritta-dhamma), a sublime state (mahaggata-dhamma) arises by way of root condition (hetu-paccaya): at the moment of rebirth-linking (paṭisandhi-kkhaṇa), dependent on the physical basis (vatthu), the sublime aggregates (khandha) arise.

Dependent on a limited state, both limited and sublime states arise by way of root condition: at the moment of rebirth-linking, dependent on the physical basis, the sublime aggregates arise; and dependent on the great primary elements, kamma-produced matter (kaṭattā-rūpa) arises.

Dependent on a sublime state, a sublime state arises by way of root condition: dependent on one sublime aggregate, three aggregates arise … two aggregates … [and so on] … at the moment of rebirth-linking … [and so on].

dependent on one sublime aggregate, three aggregates and mind-produced matter arise … pe … at the moment of rebirth-linking,

dependent on two aggregates … [and so on] … dependent on one great primary element, there arise three great primary elements … [and so on] … dependent on the great primary elements, there arise mind-produced derived matter.

[The section on] immediate, etc.:
Dependent on a limited state, a limited state arises by way of proximity condition … by way of contiguity condition.

… by way of co-nascence condition (all great primaries should be treated) … by way of mutuality condition … by way of support condition … by way of decisive support condition … by way of prenascence condition (three questions should be treated) … by way of repetition condition (three questions should be treated) … by way of kamma condition … by way of resultant condition (thirteen questions) … by way of nutriment condition … by way of faculty condition.

… by way of the condition of jhāna … by way of the condition of the path … by way of the condition of association … by way of the condition of dissociation … by way of the condition of presence … by way of the condition of absence … by way of the condition of disappearance … by way of the condition of non-disappearance.
Chapter on Enumeration.
In the pure condition of cause, there are thirteen; in object, five; in predominance, nine; in proximity, five; in contiguity, five;
in conascence, thirteen; in mutuality, seven; in dependence, thirteen; in strong-dependence, five; in prenascence, three.
In relation to repetition, there are three; in relation to kamma, thirteen; in relation to resultant, thirteen; in relation to nutriment, faculty, jhāna, and path, thirteen;

in relation to association, five; in relation to dissociation, thirteen; in relation to presence, thirteen; in relation to absence, five; in relation to disappearance, five; in relation to non-disappearance, thirteen.
This is the direct order (anuloma).

the base of infinite space (*ākāsānañcāyatana*) is related to the base of infinite consciousness (*viññāṇañcāyatana*)... the base of nothingness (*ākiñcaññāyatana*)... [is related to the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception].

It is a condition for the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception by way of object-condition (*ārammaṇa-paccaya*). Lofty aggregates (*mahaggata-khandhā*) are a condition for the knowledge of the modes of psychic power (*iddhividha-ñāṇa*),

the knowledge of penetration into others' minds (*cetopariya-ñāṇa*), the knowledge of recollection of past lives (*pubbenivāsānussati-ñāṇa*), the knowledge of the passing away and rebirth of beings according to their deeds (*yathākammūpaga-ñāṇa*),
and the knowledge of the future (*anāgataṁsa-ñāṇa*) by way of object-condition.
A sublime state is a condition for a limited state by way of object-condition:
one reviews the first jhāna … pe … one reviews the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception; one reviews the divine eye;
one reviews the divine ear-element; one reviews the knowledge of the modes of psychic power; one reviews the knowledge of penetration of minds.
One reviews the knowledge of recollection of past lives, reviews the knowledge of the passing away and reappearance of beings according to their karma, and reviews the knowledge of future existences.
One practices insight into the exalted aggregates as impermanent … [as above] … enjoys them and delights in them;
with that as object, lust arises … [as above] … grief arises.
An immeasurable state is a condition for an immeasurable state by way of object-condition: Nibbāna is a condition for the Path and the Fruition by way of object-condition.
An immeasurable state is a condition for a limited state by way of object-condition:
Noble ones, having emerged from the Path, review the Path, review the Fruition, review Nibbāna; Nibbāna is a condition for change-of-lineage (gotrabhū).
[The state] is related to purification and advertence by way of object-condition.
An immeasurable state is related to a sublime state by way of object-condition:

Noble ones know, by means of the knowledge of penetration into others' minds, the mind of one possessing an immeasurable mind; the immeasurable aggregates are related to the knowledge of penetration into others' minds and to the knowledge of recollection of past lives by way of object-condition.
It is a condition for knowledge of the future by way of object-condition.
Predominance:
A limited state is a condition for a limited state by way of predominance-condition—namely, object-predominance and conascence-predominance.
Object-predominance: Having given a gift, having undertaken virtue, and having performed the Uposatha duty, one esteems and reviews it;

one esteems and reviews former well-performed deeds. Learners esteem and review the change-of-lineage (gotrabhū), and they esteem and review purification (vodāna). The eye … [and so on] … the physical base (vatthu).
Taking limited aggregates as estimable, one relishes them and delights in them; taking them as estimable, lust arises and wrong view arises.
Co-nascent predominance: limited predominance is a condition, by way of predominance condition, for associated aggregates and for mind-originated matter.

A sublime state is a condition for a sublime state by way of predominance condition. Conascence-predominance: a sublime predominance is a condition by way of predominance condition for its associated aggregates.
A sublime state is a condition for a limited state by way of predominance condition:
as object-predominance and as conascence-predominance. Object-predominance: having taken the first jhāna as venerable …pe… [up to] the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception …pe….
... pe ... [one] esteems and reviews the divine eye ... pe ... the knowledge of future states.
Esteeming the exalted aggregates, one relishes them and delights in them; esteeming them, lust arises ... wrong view arises. Conascence-predominance:
exalted predominance is a condition, by way of predominance-condition, for mind-produced matter.
A sublime state is a condition, by way of predominance condition, for both limited and sublime states.
As co-nascent predominance: a sublime predominance is a condition, by way of predominance condition, for its associated aggregates and for mind-produced matter.
An immeasurable state is a condition for an immeasurable state by way of predominance-condition:
as object-predominance and as conascence-predominance. Object-predominance: Nibbāna is a condition for the Path and the Fruition by way of predominance-condition.
Conascence-predominance: An immeasurable predominance is a condition for its associated aggregates by way of predominance-condition.
An immeasurable state is a condition for a limited state by way of predominance condition:
as object-predominance and as conascence-predominance. Object-predominance: noble ones, having emerged from the path, esteem and review the path;
they esteem and review the fruit; they esteem and review Nibbāna; [they esteem] Nibbāna...
It is a condition for the state of lineage (*gotrabhū*) and purification (*vodāna*) by way of the predominance condition (*adhipatipaccaya*). As co-nascent predominance (*sahajātādhipati*):
the immeasurable predominance (*appamāṇādhipati*) is a condition for mind-produced matter (*cittasamuṭṭhāna-rūpa*) by way of the predominance condition.
An immeasurable state (*appamāṇa-dhamma*) is a condition for both limited (*paritta*) and immeasurable states by way of the predominance condition.
Co-nascent predominance: immeasurable predominance is a condition, by way of predominance condition, for its associated aggregates and for mind-produced matter.
Immediate...
A limited state is a condition for a limited state by way of proximity-condition (*anantara-paccaya*):
preceding limited aggregates are a condition for succeeding limited aggregates by way of proximity-condition;
adaptation is a condition for change-of-lineage; adaptation is a condition for purification; and advertence is a condition for limited aggregates by way of proximity-condition.
A limited state is a condition for a sublime state by way of proximity-condition: a limited death-consciousness is a condition for a sublime rebirth-consciousness by way of proximity-condition;
limited aggregates are a condition for a sublime emergence by way of proximity-condition;
the preparation for the first jhāna … [and so on] … up to the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception.

The preliminary work (parikamma) ... [and so on] ... the preliminary work for the divine eye ... the preliminary work for the knowledge of future states is related to the knowledge of future states by way of proximity condition (anantara-paccaya).

A limited state is related to an immeasurable state by way of proximity condition: change-of-lineage (gotrabhū) to the Path; purification (vodāna) to the Path; adaptation (anuloma) to the attainment of fruition (phala-samāpatti) is related by way of proximity condition.
A sublime state is a condition for a sublime state by way of proximity-condition: preceding sublime aggregates are a condition for succeeding sublime aggregates by way of proximity-condition.
A sublime state is a condition for a limited state by way of proximity-condition:
a sublime death-consciousness is a condition for a limited rebirth-consciousness by way of proximity-condition; a sublime life-continuum is a condition for adverting.

It is a condition by way of proximity-condition (*anantara-paccaya*). Lofty aggregates (*mahaggata-khandha*) are a condition by way of proximity-condition for a limited emergence (*paritta-vuṭṭhāna*).

A lofty state (*dhamma*) is a condition by way of proximity-condition for an immeasurable state—namely, the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception (*nevasaññānāsaññāyatana*) is a condition by way of proximity-condition for the attainment of fruition (*phala-samāpatti*) in one emerging from cessation.
An immeasurable state is a condition by way of proximity-condition for an immeasurable state—the preceding, preceding immeasurable states [are conditions for the succeeding ones].
The aggregates are related to subsequent immeasurable aggregates by way of proximity condition (*anantara-paccaya*).
The path is related to the fruit... the fruit is related to the fruit by way of proximity condition.
An immeasurable state is related to a limited state by way of proximity condition—the fruit is related to limited emergence by way of proximity condition.
An immeasurable state is a condition for a sublime state by way of proximity-condition (*anantara-paccaya*): fruition is a condition for a sublime emergence by way of proximity-condition.
The immediate-condition (*samanantara-paccaya*) is the same as the proximity-condition.
Co-nascence...
A limited state is a condition for a limited state by way of co-nascence condition:

one limited aggregate is a condition for three aggregates and for mind-produced matter by way of co-nascence condition … pe … two aggregates … pe … at the moment of rebirth-linking … pe … the aggregates are a condition for the physical basis, and the physical basis is a condition for the aggregates by way of co-nascence condition.
Condition: One great primary element … [and so on] … for non-percipient beings … [and so on].
A limited state is a conascence condition for a Lofty state: at the moment of rebirth-linking, the physical basis (vatthu) is a conascence condition for the Lofty aggregates.

A Lofty state is a conascence condition for a Lofty state: one Lofty aggregate is a conascence condition for three aggregates … two aggregates … [and so on] … at the moment of rebirth-linking … [and so on].
A sublime state is a condition for a limited state by way of co-nascence condition:

sublime aggregates are a condition for mind-produced matter by way of co-nascence condition; at the moment of rebirth-linking, sublime aggregates are a condition for kamma-produced matter by way of co-nascence condition.
A Lofty state is a condition, by way of conascence-condition, for both a limited and a Lofty state:
one Lofty aggregate is a condition, by way of conascence-condition, for three aggregates and for mind-produced matter … two aggregates … [and so on] … at the moment of rebirth-linking … [and so on].

An immeasurable state is a condition for an immeasurable state by way of co-nascence condition: one immeasurable aggregate is a condition for three aggregates by way of co-nascence condition … pe … An immeasurable state is a condition for a limited state by way of co-nascence condition:
immeasurable aggregates are a condition for mind-produced matter by way of co-nascence condition.
An immeasurable state is a condition for both a limited and an immeasurable state by way of co-nascence condition: an immeasurable …

One aggregate is a condition for three aggregates and for mind-produced matter by way of conascence-condition … pe … Limited and immeasurable states are a condition for a limited state by way of conascence-condition: immeasurable aggregates and great primaries are a condition for mind-produced matter by way of conascence-condition.
Limited and exalted states are a condition for a limited state by way of conascence-condition: exalted … [and so on].

The aggregates and the great primaries are related to mind-produced matter by way of co-nascence condition. At the moment of rebirth-linking, the sublime aggregates and the great primaries are related to kamma-produced matter by way of co-nascence condition.
Limited and sublime states are related to a sublime state by way of co-nascence condition—at the moment of rebirth-linking...
A single exalted aggregate and the [mental] basis are related to the three aggregates by way of co-nascence condition …pe….
Mutuality:
A limited state is related to a limited state by way of mutuality condition—a single limited aggregate [is related to the other three].
The three aggregates are related to one another by way of mutuality condition …pe… at the moment of rebirth-linking …pe… the aggregates are related to the physical basis,
and the physical basis is related to the aggregates, by way of mutuality condition; one great primary …pe… in the case of non-percipient beings …pe….

A limited state is a condition for a sublime state by way of mutuality-condition … pe … At the moment of rebirth-linking, the [heart-]base is a condition for the sublime aggregates by way of mutuality-condition … pe ….

A sublime state is a condition for a sublime state by way of mutuality-condition: one sublime aggregate is a condition for three aggregates by way of mutuality-condition … pe … at the moment of rebirth-linking … pe ….

A Lofty state is a condition for a Limited state by way of mutuality condition: at the moment of rebirth-linking, the Lofty aggregates are a condition for the physical basis by way of mutuality condition.
A Lofty state is a condition for both a Limited and a Lofty state by way of mutuality condition:
at the moment of rebirth-linking, one Lofty aggregate is a condition for three aggregates and the physical basis by way of mutuality condition … pe …

An immeasurable state is a condition for an immeasurable state by way of mutuality condition: one immeasurable aggregate is a condition for three aggregates by way of mutuality condition … two aggregates … [and so on] … Limited and exalted states are conditions for an exalted state by way of mutuality condition:
at the moment of rebirth-linking, one exalted aggregate together with the [heart-]base is a condition for three aggregates by way of mutuality condition … [and so on] …
A limited state is a condition for a limited state by way of the dependence condition:
one limited aggregate is a condition for three aggregates and for mind-produced matter by way of the dependence condition … [and so on] … two [aggregates].
The aggregates … [as before] … at the moment of rebirth-linking … [as before] … the aggregates are related to the physical basis by way of dependence condition;

the physical basis is related to the aggregates by way of dependence condition … one great primary element … one great primary element of non-percipient beings … the eye-base is related to eye-consciousness … the body-base is related to body-consciousness; the physical basis is related to limited aggregates by way of dependence condition.
A limited state is a condition for a sublime state by way of the dependence condition:

the physical basis is a condition for sublime aggregates by way of the dependence condition; at the moment of rebirth-linking, the physical basis is a condition for sublime aggregates by way of the dependence condition.
A limited state is a condition for an immeasurable state by way of the support-condition: the physical basis (vatthu) is a condition for immeasurable aggregates by way of the support-condition.

An exalted state is a condition for an exalted state by way of the support-condition: one exalted aggregate is a condition for three aggregates … two aggregates … [and so on] … at the moment of rebirth-linking … [and so on].
An exalted state is a condition for a limited state by way of the support-condition: exalted aggregates [are a condition for the physical basis].

It is a condition, by way of dependence-condition (*nissaya-paccaya*), for mind-originated material phenomena. At the moment of rebirth-linking, sublime aggregates (*mahaggata-khandha*) are a condition, by way of dependence-condition, for the materiality of kamma-result (*kaṭattā-rūpa*).
A sublime state is a condition, by way of dependence-condition, for both limited and sublime states—a sublime [state].
One aggregate is a condition for three aggregates and for mind-produced matter by way of the support condition … two aggregates … [and so on] … at the moment of rebirth-linking … [and so on].

An immeasurable state is a condition for an immeasurable state by way of the support condition: one immeasurable aggregate is a condition for three aggregates by way of the support condition … [and so on].
An immeasurable state is a condition for a limited state by way of the support-condition: immeasurable aggregates are a condition for mind-produced matter by way of the support-condition.
An immeasurable state is a condition for both a limited and an immeasurable state by way of the support-condition:
one immeasurable aggregate is a condition for three aggregates and mind-produced matter by way of the support-condition … pe …

Limited and immeasurable states are related to a limited state by way of dependence condition: immeasurable aggregates and great primaries are related to mind-produced matter by way of dependence condition.

Limited and immeasurable states are related to an immeasurable state by way of dependence condition: one immeasurable aggregate and the [heart-]base are related to three aggregates by way of dependence condition; ... two aggregates ... etc. ... [and so on].
Limited and sublime states are related to a limited state by way of the dependence condition:

sublime aggregates and great primaries are related to mind-produced matter by way of the dependence condition; at the moment of rebirth-linking, sublime aggregates and great primaries are related to kamma-produced matter by way of the dependence condition.
Limited and exalted states are related to an exalted state by way of the dependence condition:
one exalted aggregate and the [heart-]base are related to three aggregates by way of the dependence condition …pe… at the moment of rebirth-linking,
one exalted aggregate and the [heart-]base are related to three aggregates by way of the dependence condition.

By way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*), a limited phenomenon (*paritta-dhamma*) is a condition for a limited phenomenon: namely, object-decisive support (*ārammaṇūpanissaya*).
Proximity-predominance condition, natural-predominance condition … [as above] … Natural-predominance condition:
depending on limited faith, one gives a gift, undertakes virtue, performs the Uposatha duty, arouses insight, conceives conceit, adopts wrong view;
[depending on] limited virtue … [as above] … wisdom … lust … [as above] … aspiration, bodily pleasure.
... [as before] ... depending on a lodging, one gives a gift, observes virtue, ... [as before] ... observes the Uposatha, ... [as before] ...
arouses insight, kills a living being, ... [as before] ... causes a schism in the Saṅgha. Limited faith, ... [as before] ... wisdom, lust, ...
[as before] ... aspiration, bodily pleasure, ... [as before] ... the lodging, [are related] to limited faith, ... [as before] ... wisdom, to lust, ... [as before] ... to aspiration.
Bodily pleasure is a condition for bodily pleasure, and bodily pain is a condition for bodily pain, by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*).

Wholesome and unwholesome kamma is a condition for its result (*vipāka*) by way of decisive support condition. Killing is a condition for killing by way of decisive support condition (the cycle should be completed). Matricide is a condition for matricide by way of decisive support condition.
Condition. (The wheel should be constructed similar to that of the wholesome triad.

A limited state is a condition for a sublime state by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*)—namely, proximity-decisive support (*anantara-upanissaya*) and natural decisive support (*pakatūpanissaya*) …pe… Natural decisive support: having relied upon limited faith as a decisive support, one enters a sublime meditative absorption (*jhāna*).

One arouses [a state]; one arouses direct knowledge; one arouses meditative attainment. Depending on limited virtue … pe … wisdom … lust … pe … and depending on a lodging-place, one arouses exalted jhāna, arouses direct knowledge, and arouses meditative attainment.
Limited faith … pe … depending on a lodging-place as a decisive support condition for exalted faith … pe … wisdom … [it acts as a decisive support condition].

Condition: The preliminary practice (*parikamma*) for the first jhāna …pe… the preliminary practice for the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception (*nevasaññānāsaññāyatana*) is a decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*) for the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception.
The preliminary practice for the divine eye (*dibba-cakkhu*) …pe… the preliminary practice for the knowledge of future existences (*anāgataṃsa-ñāṇa*) …pe….

A limited state is a condition for an immeasurable state by way of decisive support condition (upanissaya-paccaya)—namely, as proximity-decisive support (anantara-upanissaya) and natural decisive support (pakata-upanissaya)… [as appropriate]… Natural decisive support:
relying on limited faith, one generates immeasurable jhāna, generates the Path, or attains the fruition-attainment (phala-samāpatti). Limited virtue… [as appropriate]… limited wisdom… [likewise].
Depending on lust … [and so on] … aspiration … bodily pleasure … [and so on] … lodging-place,

one arouses immeasurable jhāna, arouses the path, and arouses the attainment of fruition. Limited faith … [and so on] … lodging-place is related to immeasurable faith … [and so on] … wisdom, to the path, and to the attainment of fruition, by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*).
The preparation for the first path is related to the first path ... [and so on] ...
the preparation for the fourth path is related to the fourth path by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*).
A sublime state is related to a sublime state by way of decisive support condition: as immediate decisive support (*anantara-upanissaya*), ...
Natural decisive support … [as above] … Natural decisive support:

depending on exalted faith, one arouses exalted jhāna, arouses direct knowledge, and arouses attainment. Depending on exalted virtue … [as above] … depending on exalted wisdom, one arouses exalted jhāna, arouses direct knowledge, and arouses attainment. Exalted faith.
...pe... wisdom is related to exalted faith ...pe... to wisdom by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*).

The first jhāna is related to the second jhāna ...pe... the base of nothingness (*ākiñcaññāyatana*) is related to the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception (*nevasaññānāsaññāyatana*) by way of decisive support condition.
An exalted state is related to a limited state by way of decisive support condition—namely, as object-decisive-support (*ārammaṇūpanissaya*).
Proximity-predominance condition, natural-predominance condition … [as above] … Natural-predominance condition:

depending on exalted faith, one gives a gift, undertakes virtue, performs the Uposatha duty, arouses insight, conceives conceit, adopts a wrong view; [depending on] exalted virtue … [and so on] … depending on wisdom, one gives a gift … [and so on] … [arouses] insight.
[It] causes [it] to arise …pe… sublime faith …pe… wisdom is a condition for limited faith …pe… wisdom …pe… bodily pleasure,
and bodily pain, by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*).
A sublime state is a condition for an immeasurable state by way of decisive support condition— namely, proximity-decisive support (*anantara-upanissaya*).

Natural decisive support … [as above] … Natural decisive support: depending on sublime faith as a decisive support, one arouses immeasurable jhāna, arouses the path, and arouses the attainment of fruition.
Depending on sublime virtue … [as above] … and wisdom as a decisive support, one arouses immeasurable jhāna, arouses the path, and arouses the attainment of fruition.
Lofty faith … pe … wisdom is related to immeasurable faith … pe … wisdom, to the path, and to the attainment of fruition,
by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*).
An immeasurable state is related to an immeasurable state by way of decisive support condition— namely, object-decisive support (*ārammaṇūpanissaya*).
Proximity-decisive-support, natural-decisive-support … [and so on] … Natural-decisive-support:
depending upon immeasurable faith, one generates immeasurable jhāna, generates the path, and attains the fruition-attainment.
Depending upon immeasurable virtue … [and so on] … depending upon immeasurable wisdom, one generates immeasurable jhāna, generates the path, and attains the fruition-attainment.
It produces [them]. Immeasurable faith … pe … wisdom is a condition for immeasurable faith … pe … wisdom by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*).
The first path is a condition for the second path … pe … the third path is a condition for the fourth path;
the path is a condition for the attainment of fruition (*phala-samāpatti*) by way of decisive support condition.
An immeasurable state is a condition for a limited state by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*):
as object-decisive support, proximity-decisive support, and natural decisive support ... [etc. ... Natural decisive support:

relying on an immeasurable confidence (*saddhā*), one gives a gift, undertakes virtue ... [etc. ... performs the observance-day duty (*uposathakamma*), and arouses insight (*vipassanā*). An immeasurable virtue ... [etc. ...
Relying on wisdom (paññā), one gives a gift, observes virtue, performs the Uposatha duty, practices insight (vipassanā), or develops immeasurable faith;
thus, wisdom is a condition for limited faith, limited virtue, limited concentration, limited wisdom, bodily happiness, and bodily pain by way of the decisive support condition (upanissaya-paccaya).
The attainment of fruition (phala-samāpatti) is a condition for bodily happiness by way of the decisive support condition.

Condition: The Noble Ones, depending upon the Path as a decisive support (upanissaya), practice insight into formations as impermanent … [and so on] … The Path is a condition for the Noble Ones’ analytical knowledge of meaning (atthapaṭisambhidā) … [and so on] … for the analytical knowledge of expression (dhammapaṭisambhidā) … for the analytical knowledge of philology (niruttipaṭisambhidā) … and for proficiency in what is possible and impossible (ṭhānāṭhānakosalla), by way of being a decisive support condition.
An immeasurable state is a condition for a sublime state by way of being a decisive support condition—namely, proximity-decisive support (anantarūpanissaya).
Natural strong-dependence … [as above] … Natural strong-dependence:

depending on immeasurable faith, one arouses sublime jhāna, arouses direct knowledge, arouses attainment. Depending on immeasurable virtue … [and so on for the other factors] … depending on wisdom, one arouses sublime jhāna, arouses direct knowledge, arouses attainment. Immeasurable faith.
… pe … wisdom is a condition for exalted faith … pe … for wisdom by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*).
Noble ones, relying upon the Path as a decisive support, give rise to an unarisen attainment and enter an arisen attainment.
Pre-arising (*purejāta*).
A limited state is a condition for a limited state by way of prenascence condition—namely, object-prenascence and base-prenascence.
Regarding object-prenascence: one contemplates the eye as impermanent ... [and so on] ... with insight, relishes it, and delights in it;
taking that as an object, lust arises ... [and so on] ... grief arises. [The same applies to] the ear ... [and so on] ... regarding the base as impermanent.
...pe... sorrow arises. The visible-object base is a pre-arising condition for eye-consciousness ...pe... the tangible-object base is a pre-arising condition for body-consciousness.
As for the pre-arising condition of the physical basis (*vatthupurejāta*): the eye-base is a pre-arising condition for eye-consciousness ...pe...
the body-base is a pre-arising condition for body-consciousness; the physical basis is a pre-arising condition for limited aggregates.
A limited state is a condition for a sublime state by way of prenascence condition—namely, object-prenascence and base-prenascence.
Object-prenascence: one sees a visible form with the divine eye; one hears a sound with the divine ear-element.
Base-prenascence: the physical basis is a condition for the sublime aggregates by way of prenascence condition.

A limited state is a condition for an immeasurable state by way of prenascence condition. As a base-prenascence: the physical base is a condition for immeasurable aggregates by way of prenascence condition.
Postnascence:
A limited state is a condition for a limited state by way of postnascence condition. Postnascent limited aggregates are a condition for this prenascent body by way of postnascence condition.
A sublime state is a condition for a limited state by way of postnascence condition: postnascent sublime aggregates are a condition for this prenascent body by way of postnascence condition.

An immeasurable state is a condition for a limited state by way of postnascence condition: postnascent immeasurable aggregates are a condition for this prenascent body by way of postnascence condition.
Repetition...
A limited state is a condition for a limited state by way of the condition of repetition (*āsevanapaccaya*):

preceding limited aggregates are a condition for succeeding limited aggregates... [and so on] ...adaptation (*anuloma*) is a condition for change-of-lineage (*gotrabhū*), and adaptation is a condition for purification (*vodāna*), by way of the condition of repetition.
A limited state is a condition for an exalted state by way of the condition of repetition (*āsevanapaccaya*).

The preparation (*parikamma*) for the first jhāna is a condition for that same [jhāna] by way of the condition of repetition …pe… the preparation for the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception is a condition for that same [base] by way of the condition of repetition.
The preparation for the divine eye …pe… for the knowledge of future lives.
Preparatory work (*parikamma*) is related to knowledge of future states (*anāgataṃsañāṇa*) by way of the condition of repetition (*āsevanapaccaya*).

A limited state (*paritta dhamma*) is related to an immeasurable state (*appamāṇa dhamma*) by way of the condition of repetition: change-of-lineage (*gotrabhu*) is related to the path (*magga*) ... purification (*vodāna*) is related to the path by way of the condition of repetition.

An exalted state (*mahaggata dhamma*) is related to an exalted state by way of the condition of repetition: preceding exalted aggregates are related to succeeding exalted aggregates ... [etc. ... by way of the condition of repetition.
Limited state is related to limited state by way of kamma condition: as conascent and as asynchronous.
As conascent: limited volition is related to its associated aggregates and to mind-produced matter by way of kamma condition.
Condition: At the moment of rebirth-linking, limited volition is a condition, by way of kamma-condition, for the associated aggregates and for the material phenomena produced by kamma (kaṭattā-rūpa).
